title: Distance-time graphs: how a line tells speed
learning_objective: Read speed as the steepness of a distance-time graph and compare two motions by their lines.

sections.title: A journey becomes a line
sections.narration: A cyclist rides along a straight road. Every second, we note how far she has come and mark it in a graph: time runs to the right, distance runs upwards. The marks line up, and her whole journey becomes one rising line.
sections.visual_plan: A coordinate system with time on the x axis and distance on the y axis. Points appear one per second and a straight line grows through them.

sections.title: Steeper means faster
sections.narration: Now a second cyclist starts at the same moment, but covers more distance in every second. Her line climbs more steeply. That is the whole secret of this graph: the steeper the line, the faster the motion. The line does not show the road. It shows the progress.
sections.visual_plan: Two lines from the origin with clearly different steepness. A moving point on each line advances during the same time span; the steeper line's point gets further.

sections.title: Reading the speed
sections.narration: Let us read the first cyclist's speed straight from the graph. Between second one and second four, three seconds pass, and the distance grows by six metres. Speed is distance divided by time: six metres divided by three seconds gives two metres per second. Every second, two metres.
sections.visual_plan: The formula builds up in three large steps: the general ratio, the values read from the graph with units, and the result highlighted.

sections.title: A pause in the journey
sections.purpose: One more reading: the flat line
sections.narration: Sometimes the line neither rises nor falls, and for a while it runs perfectly flat. Time still passes, but the distance does not change. A flat line means the cyclist has stopped for a rest at the roadside.
sections.visual_plan: The line rises, then a clearly marked horizontal segment follows before it rises again. The flat segment is highlighted while the rest of the line stays muted.

sections.title: Reading the whole story
sections.purpose: Closure: takeaway, recall question, and a deliberate ending
sections.narration: Back to our cyclist: her whole journey became one line, and you can read it now. Steeper means faster, and flat means resting. One question to keep: when one line ends higher but another is steeper, which cyclist is faster? Say it in one sentence. Then you can read any distance-time graph.
sections.visual_plan: The key statement and a small graph with both lines appear. The thinking question then stays large and calm on screen, and the closing line fades in beneath it.
sections.check_prompt: Explain in one sentence why the steeper line belongs to the faster cyclist even when the other line ends higher.

recap_cards.title: Steepness is speed
recap_cards.message: The steeper the line in a distance-time graph, the faster the motion.
recap_cards.visual_plan: Two lines of different steepness from the origin, the steeper one marked as faster.

recap_cards.title: Speed as a ratio
recap_cards.message: Distance covered divided by the time taken, always with its unit.
recap_cards.visual_plan: The formula next to the values read from the graph.

recap_cards.title: Worked example
recap_cards.message: Six metres in three seconds gives two metres per second.
recap_cards.visual_plan: Graph with the time span and distance gain marked, next to the calculation.
